newsitem.title: USA: N.J. bond dispute headed to state Supreme Court.
newsitem.headline: N.J. bond dispute headed to state Supreme Court.

text.p: New Jersey Attorney General Peter Verniero said Tuesday he would take a dispute over the state's $2.8 billion pension bond deal directly to the state Supreme Court, bypassing the appellate division.
A former Democratic legislator, Alan J. Karcher, is appealing Judge Phillip Carchman's earlier ruling upholding the sale. Karcher also asked the high court to hear a direct appeal.
Karcher had argued that the state must obtain voter approval in a referendum for the taxable bond deal, which Merrill Lynch & Co plans to price Wednesday.

The pension bond law authorizes the state treasurer to contract with the Economic Development Authority to sell the bonds in return for the pledge to pay the debt service from annual appropriations. It also helps balance the annual budget.

Carchman ruled that because the bonds are sold by the EDA, there is no constitutional obligation on the state to repay -- only a moral and practical consideration. That means the voter referendum required for state-supported debt does not apply, the court ruled.
